🪄
Custom percentage scoringInstead of the standard present ÷ total formula, each mark can add or deduct your chosen percentage points.
When enabled for a category, score = starting score + Present gains − Absent deductions, clamped to 0–100%. Changing or removing a mark recalculates from dated records, so the same mark is never counted twice.
📘
Regular subjectsLectures and non-lab classes

Applied to each dated mark for regular subjects.

🧪
Lab subjectsPractical sessions and labs

Lab rules are independent of regular subjects.

Custom scoring is off. Attendance is calculated from saved marks: Present ÷ (Present + Absent) × 100%. Subjects without saved marks show “—”.

Choose a backup folder

Keep monthly copies somewhere safe outside the app.

Pick an existing folder or create a new one named Attendance Trackie Backups. Monthly copies will use dated JSON filenames.
Direct folder writes need an Android folder-picker bridge. True monthly writes while the app is closed also need a native background worker. Internal monthly snapshots work regardless.

Backup help

Quick answers, without cluttering Settings.

Q. Which files can I import?

A. A backup exported by Attendance Trackie as .json. You can also import a .txt file if it contains the same JSON text. CSV, Excel, screenshots, and ZIP files are not import formats.

Q. What should the file look like?

A. The simplest option is to use Export backup. It creates a complete file with a data object, semester dates, subject settings, and dated class statuses. Keep the exported contents unchanged.

Q. Can I import an older or plain backup?

A. The app accepts its wrapped backup format and a raw app-data object with subjects and semester dates. Invalid or incomplete files are rejected before replacing your current data.

Q. Where do automatic backups go?

A. A monthly copy is stored in private app storage. If a folder was selected and your APK builder exposes the backup bridge, an additional dated JSON file is written to that folder. Export a manual copy before uninstalling.
